title: The minute

caption:
Part 3. The old clockmaker explains what they've held off for 27 years. 🕰️

Original fiction. Part 4 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Theo found himself in a photo from last year's party in Merrow Falls, a party he had never been to.
scenes.image: an old party photograph lying on a desk under lamplight, a grey-coated figure in the crowd

scenes.narration: The counting stopped at fifty-nine. It always does, said an old woman behind him.
scenes.image: a very old woman in a shawl standing in a snowy doorway, lamplight behind her

scenes.narration: Her name was Delia Marsh. She ran the clock shop. She was the only person in town who still wound anything.
scenes.image: a very old woman in a cluttered clock repair shop surrounded by stopped antique clocks

scenes.narration: On New Year's Eve, 1999, she said, the whole town heard something coming. Not a sound. A pressure. Like the sky leaning in.
scenes.image: a heavy low winter sky pressing down over a small town at night, eerie pale glow

scenes.narration: So at 11:59 I stopped them. Every clock. Every watch. I didn't stop time. I just stopped letting it in.
scenes.image: an old woman's wrinkled hands holding a brass pocket watch open in lamplight

scenes.narration: Theo asked: holding it off from what? She said: whatever comes at midnight. We never learned its name. We never wanted to.
scenes.image: close-up of the old clockmaker's eyes, tired and frightened

scenes.narration: And the photo, Theo said. Me. Last year. She sighed. You've come before, dear. Every year. And every year you forget.
scenes.image: a man in a grey coat sitting stiffly on a stool among silent clocks

scenes.narration: And every year, she said, you get a little closer to midnight before you go.
scenes.image: a dark snowy road at night with a single pair of headlights approaching a town

scenes.narration: Theo looked at the hundreds of clocks on her walls. All still. All silent.
scenes.image: a wall covered in dozens of antique clocks, all silent, in warm lamplight

scenes.narration: Then, in the hush, one of them began to tick. Delia went white. It wasn't on her wall. It was on Theo's wrist.
scenes.image: close-up of a silver wristwatch on a man's wrist in lamplight, the second hand blurred in motion
